limits_note: Up to 10 simultaneous connections per Storage Box account; snapshot slots are 10/20/30/40 for BX11/BX21/BX31/BX41; files sit on RAID disks of a single host server and the data is not mirrored onto other servers.
reliability_note: LowEndTalk regularly reports throughput is node-dependent (sub-30 Mbit/s on bad nodes) and that Hetzner's automatic usage-anomaly detection has disconnected boxes triggered by third-party traffic; 10-connection cap is the real binding constraint for parallel ranged GETs.

extras.document_section: S3-compatible object storage below the big three
extras.verified_at_basis: Your files on Storage Boxes are safeguarded with a RAID configuration which can withstand several drive failures.
extras.quota_verbatim: 1 TB (BX11) / 5 TB (BX21) / 10 TB (BX31) / 20 TB (BX41); no per-file cap published, 100 sub-accounts, 10 snapshots
extras.limits_verbatim: 10 concurrent connections (hard, product page); 10 snapshots; RAID on one host and explicitly 'data is not mirrored onto other servers' — single-site durability, not object-store 11-nines.
extras.egress_verbatim: Verbatim, plan table: "Traffic | - Unlimited". Unlimited outbound, no cap tier, no overage SKU exists for this product.
extras.chaining_verbatim: Mounts directly to AList/OpenList via WebDAV or SFTP, or to a Hetzner Cloud VM which then fronts S3/HTTP behind Cloudflare — the forum-documented pattern for turning unmetered Storage Box traffic into a served HTTP origin.
extras.tooling_verbatim: rclone (explicitly listed), restic, borg, rsync; no S3 API
extras.interface_verbatim: SFTP, FTP/FTPS, SCP, rsync-over-SSH, WebDAV, Samba/CIFS, HTTPS; BorgBackup and Restic native
extras.price_verbatim: $2.28/TB at 20 TB (EUR 40.60 = $45.61); $2.45/TB at 5 TB (EUR 10.90 = $12.24); $3.59/TB at 1 TB (EUR 3.20 = $3.59). Cheapest genuine unlimited-egress storage found.
extras.agent_focus: Cheap-paid lane: S3-compatible object storage outside AWS/Azure/GCP/Alibaba/Cloudflare/B2/IDrive-e2. Target = true $/TB/month floor with free-or-generous egress, computed at the 5 TB and 20 TB tiers. EUR->USD at 1.1234 (frankfurter.app, 2026-10-21).

binding_note: the per-object cap sets the shard size and therefore the object count; it bounds the total more tightly than any headline quota
